newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Games organisers were warned yesterday some disabled athletes may attempt to cheat the system by hiding their abilities leading into the Sydney 2000 Paralympics. Games staff were briefed by orthopaedic surgeon Dr John Bourke on the complicated system ofclassification in disabled sports. Page 20.

Soccer Australia chairman David Hill said yesterday soccer could become fully professional here within five years, with Victorian clubs becoming professional next year, pressuring other clubs to follow suit. Page 23.

The NBL has been caught by surprise by League chairman Mal Speed's application for the Australian Rugby League chief executive's position, to be announced today. Several NBL directors told the Australian they knew nothing of Speed's intentions. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's top domestic soccer players will be better off from next season with the formation of the Players Commission - comprising representatives of Soccer Australia, the premiership clubs and the players' union. The Commission, the first sporting comission of its time in Australia, aims primarily to provide a decent living for national league players. Page 45.

Following a meeting with Olympic Games officials yesterday, Australian Baseball Federation officials say they now expect a permanent purpose-built stadium to be constructed in Sydney for the 2000 games. After months of fighting an agreement has been reached at a meeting of the Sydney organising committee's Sports Commission, according to Baseball Federation executive director John Ostermeyer and leading Olympic official Phil Coles. Page 45.

Only two candidates, Balmain president Neil Whittaker and National Basketball League chairman Mal Speed, are under consideration to follow John Quayle as Australian Rugby League chief executive, with the victor being announced today. The role is seen as vital to the future of the game. Page 46.
THE AGE

Champion jockey Darren Beadman was too ill to return to Sydney from Hong Kong yesterday, continuing his mixed luck overseas. The virus has left his participation in the inaugural state-of-origin jockeys' series in Sydney and Melbourne at the weekend in dubt. Page C10.

This season's Prime Minister's XI yesterday handed the West Indies their sixth successive loss on this tour, captained by cricket veteran Allan Border. The Australian A side waits to cap off the Windies losing streak on Friday in Melbourne. Page C12.

Emma George broke the world record for women's indoor pole-vaulting yesterday, clearing 4.40 metres - a remarkable 12 centimetres higher than China's Sun Caiyun's 4.28 metres. The feat was performed in Camberwell Grammar's gym, with George's first jump beaking the Australian record and the second jump achieving a place in the record books. Page C12.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian women's under-20 basketball team, the Gems, will leave on Christmas Day to start one of the highest standard tours ever undertaken by a national junior basketball squad. In preparation to defend their world junior championship, the team wil compete against teams in England, Russia, Spain and Japan. Page 78.

Australian Rugby Union chief executive John O'Neill has said it is unlikely Australia's top rugby players will play club football next season in a bid to ensure they avoid burnout, a day after the unbeaten Wallabies returned from their tour of Europe. Pae 79.

The sudden resignation of Sky Channel chief executive Bill North will not change the process of setting up Australia's first pay-TV racing channel, according to senior officials from the Victoria Racing Club, Australian Jockey Club and Sky Channel itself. Page 81.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH
Sydney yacht skipper David Witt is the first from the 18-footer ranks to buy an Australian-designed and built 49-er. The yacht is set to make its debut at the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Page 77.

After missing a place in Australia's relay sprint team at the Atlanta Olympics, former national sprint champion Shane Naylor is aiming to launch his Rugby League career at the World Sevens in Sydney in February. Naylor has already played a few games in Melbourne, but he says his loyalty is with North Sydney who sponsored him during his athletic career. Page 77.

Winmalee High School shot-put thrower Katrina Steele, the youngest member of the Australian track and field team at the World Junior Championships, has led New South Wales' victorious charge at the Pacific Schools Games in Perth this week. Steele took out three gold, one silver and one bronze at the international meet, which is also doubling as the Australian All Schools Athletics Championships. Page 79.
